summary: Backend-only regression for the NEW / MODIFIED surfaces added on top of the previously-refactored backend. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_new_features.py covering: Recently Practiced (practice-log + recently-practiced), Leaderboard Prizes (public list + admin CRUD + oversize/rank/range guards), Admin Leaderboard controls (hide/unhide, hidden-users listing, per-user completion reset preserving wishlist, season lifecycle w/ archive + season pointer honored by /api/leaderboard, DELETE season restores all-time view), Instructor Trend (weeks clamping, shape, ascending order, totals=sum), plus a fast sanity smoke of the previous surfaces (3 seed logins, /dances >200, /leaderboard, /instructor/dashboard, /song-preview). Result: 45/46 PASSED. ONE FAILURE — /api/instructor/trend?weeks=0 does NOT clamp to 2 as the spec requires; it returns 8 (default) instead. Root cause: `int(weeks or 8)` in routes/dashboard.py:226 treats 0 as falsy and short-circuits to the default 8 BEFORE the clamp. The clamp code `max(2, min(26, ...))` never sees the intended value 0. weeks=99 (upper bound) works correctly (returns 26). All other newly-added endpoints behave correctly, including season epoch honoring in /api/leaderboard (after season reset, prior completions disappear from range=all).

minor.issue: weeks=0 returns 8 weeks instead of clamping to 2. Spec says 0 → 2. Root cause: `int(weeks or 8)` in routes/dashboard.py:226 — Python treats 0 as falsy, so `0 or 8` becomes 8 BEFORE the max(2, ...) clamp. Fix: change to `int(weeks) if weeks is not None else 8` (or drop the `or 8` and rely on the default arg + max/min). weeks=99 clamps to 26 correctly.

rca_of_issue: BUG: GET /api/instructor/trend?weeks=0 returns 8 weeks (default) instead of the expected 2. Reproduction: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <instructor_token>' '$BASE/api/instructor/trend?weeks=0'` → len(weeks) == 8. Root cause: line 226 of routes/dashboard.py uses `int(weeks or 8)` — because Python treats integer 0 as falsy, `0 or 8` evaluates to 8, and the intended `max(2, min(26, 0)) = 2` clamp never runs. Mitigation (main agent to apply): replace with `raw = 8 if weeks is None else int(weeks); weeks = max(2, min(26, raw))`. This preserves the default-when-missing behavior while letting 0 clamp up to 2 as the spec requires. Similar pattern (integer-with-falsy-default) appears in routes/activity.py:70 `int(limit or 10)` — that endpoint's spec doesn't require limit=0 to clamp to 1 explicitly, and the test test_limit_clamping only asserts `<= 1`, so it currently passes; but it's the same anti-pattern and worth harmonizing.
